title: Priming Base Models for Agentic Post-Training: An Open Midtraining Recipe
data_curation: A ~380B-unique-token blend of mostly natural software-engineering data plus a bounded share of agent traces: Issue-PR 216.9B unique tokens (40.8% of blend; 12.1M merged PRs from GitHub repos with >=10 stars, issue-PR pairs checked by a structured LLM judge with seven failure modes and repaired or removed), dependency-connected repositories 104.1B (20%; from the Nemotron 3 pretraining corpus, 14 languages, kept only if >=20% of code files import another file, 10% for Ruby, serialized README-first in depth-first import order, packed at 256K; Python upweighted to 31%), agentic traces 39.4B (10%; >1M trajectories, ~500K queries, 30M tool calls from >10 scaffolds incl. OpenHands, Codex, Claude Code, Terminus, SWE-agent, with the best traces reserved for SFT), diff data 16.0B (3%; 733,705 multi-file edits and 377,618 code-evolution documents from 6,550 repos), build/CI logs 6.5B (1.2%; LogHub, GHALogs, 632 LLM-written diagnosis examples), 20% pretraining replay and 5% long-context data. All sources are permissively licensed, decontaminated against SWE-bench and Terminal-Bench, secret-redacted, and loss-masked on hashes, timestamps and delimiters; trace filtering drops leakage, unfinished runs, malformed calls and loops (~1%).
curriculum: Midtraining is inserted between pretraining (8K context) and post-training: hundreds of billions of tokens at 256K context, ideally before the final 1M long-context stage, so that much agentic learning moves out of SFT and SFT can stay short to preserve later RL trainability. Traces are capped at 10-15% of the blend to avoid SFT-like overfitting, and replay is fixed at 20% (40% gave no clear benefit). LR warms up briefly then stays constant (5e-5 for Lightning with 32K-sequence warmup, 1e-5 for Super with 30K). In experiments, scaling runs start from the 1M long-context checkpoint and go straight to SFT, either short (33B tokens) or full (100B tokens; ~430K agentic trajectories mostly generated by GLM-5.2, LR 2e-5 cosine to 5e-6). A ~9B-token long-context stage restores Super's RULER@1M from 33.0 to 81.0; a 20-step GRPO check (14 verifiable environments, 256 prompts x 16 generations, LR 1e-6) follows full SFT on Lightning-8K.
method: An open, ablated midtraining recipe for agentic coding, applied to Nemotron 3.5 Lightning-30B-A3B (up to 500B tokens) and Nemotron 3.5 Super-120B-A12B (65B and 280B tokens). Training uses Megatron-LM on GB300 GPUs, packed 256K sequences, global batch 64 sequences, Adam (0.9, 0.95), weight decay 0.1, grad clip 1.0, BF16, inter-document attention masking, and the models' two MTP layers kept (loss weight 0.1 / 0.3). Key design choices: agent traces are rendered in the Nemotron chat template while everything else stays in natural format; only assistant turns are trained, since training on tool responses cut SWE-bench Verified pass@1 from 37.8 to 27.5; LR trades agentic gains against general capability: on Lightning-8K, warming up to 5e-5 dropped MATH-500 from 79.7 to 61.7 even with replay, while 1e-5 gave smaller post-SFT gains in early runs, hence 5e-5 for Lightning and 1e-5 for Super. Recipe decisions are judged by identical short/full SFT runs because base-model proxies (bits-per-byte, LoCoDiff, RepoBench) did not reliably predict post-training results.
eval_metrics: After identical SFT: SWE-bench Verified (500), Multilingual (300) and Pro (731) in OpenHands (3 rollouts, 200 turns, 250 for Pro), Terminal-Bench 2.0/2.1 (89 tasks) in Terminus-2 (8 rollouts), DeepSWE (4 runs) and a BrowseComp subset, reporting pass@1 and pass@k at temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, plus a six-harness sweep. Base-model metrics are LoCoDiff exact match/edit distance, RepoBench, and repository and trace bits-per-byte; regression checks use MMLU, MMLU-Pro, GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval, MBPP, commonsense suites and RULER. Lightning at 500B tokens: SWE-V 60.7 -> 64.5, Multilingual 55.8 -> 62.8, Pro 32.0 -> 35.5, TB 22.6 -> 23.6, LoCoDiff exact 0.0 -> 26.8%. Super at 280B: DeepSWE 11.7 -> 15.7, SWE-V 72.9 -> 74.3, BrowseComp 61.8 -> 64.8, but Multilingual and Pro end 1.1 and 2.1 points below base.
key_results: On Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, 500B midtraining tokens improve SWE-bench Verified/Multilingual/Pro by 3.8/7.0/3.5 points after identical full SFT, and on Nemotron 3.5 Super 280B tokens raise DeepSWE from 11.7 to 15.7 and SWE-bench Verified from 72.9 to 74.3. Midtraining improves every agent harness tested (+8.6 SWE-V and +6.8 Terminal-Bench 2.1 averaged across harnesses on Super after short SFT; +11.6 SWE-V across six harnesses on Lightning-8K), and agent traces supply most of the gain over natural data alone.
evolution_note: The paper opens up the midtraining stage that Qwen3-Coder-Next, GLM-5, Kimi-Dev, daVinci-Dev and Composer 2 describe only at a high level, publishing per-source construction, blend weights and ablations. It reacts to evidence that very long SFT stages hurt later RL trainability by moving natural SWE data and lower-tier traces into a 256K pretraining-style stage. Its preliminary 20-step GRPO run shows only that the midtrained advantage survives the start of RL, so whether midtraining increases what RL can add is still open; the authors plan to scale the trace corpus (already ~90B tokens) and move reasoning/chat data into midtraining.
